butir.teks: On the Rational Evidences

Know that what is sought from this chapter is knowledge of the excellence of knowledge and its preciousness. As long as excellence is not understood in itself and what is meant by it is not established, it is not possible to know its existence as an attribute of knowledge or of any other quality. For he has strayed from the path who hopes to know whether Zayd is wise or not while he has not yet understood the meaning of wisdom and its reality.

Excellence (fadila) is taken from fadl, which is increase. When two things share in one matter and one of them is distinguished by an additional measure, it is said that it excels the other and that it has the superiority over it, whenever its increase is in what constitutes the perfection of that thing. For example, it is said that the horse is better than the donkey, meaning that it shares with the donkey the strength of carrying and exceeds it in the strength of charging and retreating, in swiftness of running, and in beauty of form. So if a donkey were supposed to be distinguished by an additional growth, it would not be said that it is better, because that is an increase in the body and a deficiency in the inner nature, and it is not part of perfection at all. An animal is sought for its inner nature and its attributes, not for its body. So when you have understood this, it will not be hidden from you that knowledge is an excellence if you take it in relation to the other attributes, just as the horse has an excellence if you take it in relation to the other animals. Indeed, swiftness of running is an excellence in the horse, but it is not an excellence in the absolute sense. Knowledge is an excellence in itself and in the absolute sense, without relation to anything, for it is an attribute of the perfection of Allah, glorified is He, and through it the angels and the prophets were ennobled. Indeed, the clever among horses is better than the dull one, so that is an excellence in the absolute sense, without relation.

Know that a precious, desired thing divides into what is sought for the sake of something else, what is sought for its own sake, and what is sought both for the sake of something else and for its own sake together. What is sought for its own sake is nobler and more excellent than what is sought for the sake of something else. What is sought for the sake of something else is the dirhams and dinars, for they are two stones with no benefit in them, and were it not that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, made it easy to meet needs by means of them, they and the pebbles would be on one level.
And what is sought for its own sake is happiness in the Hereafter and the delight of looking at the face of Allah Most High.

And what is sought both for its own sake and for the sake of something else is like the soundness of the body. For the soundness of the leg, for example, is sought insofar as it is the soundness of the body from pain, and it is sought for walking with it and for reaching aims and needs. In this respect, when you look at knowledge, you will see it delightful in itself, so that it is sought for its own sake, and you will find it a means to the abode of the Hereafter and its happiness, and a way to nearness to Allah Most High, and that nearness cannot be reached except through knowledge. The greatest of things in rank for the human being is eternal happiness, and the most excellent of things is what is a means to it, and it will never be reached except through knowledge and action, and action cannot be reached except through knowledge of how to act. So the root of happiness in this world and the Hereafter is knowledge, and it is therefore the most excellent of deeds. And how could it not be, when the excellence of a thing is also known by the nobility of its fruit, and you have known that the fruit of knowledge is nearness to the Lord of the worlds, joining the horizon of the angels, and keeping company with the Highest Assembly.

This is in the Hereafter. As for this world, it is honour, dignity, the enforcement of judgment over kings, and the necessity of respect in natural dispositions, so much so that the dull-witted among the Turks and the coarse among the Arabs find their natures innately disposed to revere their elders for being distinguished by additional knowledge gained from experience. Indeed, even the beast, by its nature, reveres the human being, because it senses that the human being is distinguished by a perfection that goes beyond its own rank. This is the excellence of knowledge in the absolute sense. Then the sciences differ, as its explanation will come, and their excellences inevitably differ as they differ.

As for the excellence of teaching and learning, it is evident from what we have mentioned. For if knowledge is the most excellent of matters, then learning it is seeking what is most excellent, and teaching it is imparting what is most excellent. The explanation is that the aims of people are gathered in religion and this world, and there is no order for religion except through the order of this world, for this world is the farm of the Hereafter, and it is the instrument that leads to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for whoever takes it as an instrument, and a lodging for whoever takes it as a settled abode and homeland. And the affair of this world is not ordered except through the works of human beings.
And their works, trades, and crafts are confined to three divisions.
The first of them is foundations without which the world cannot subsist, and they are four: farming, which is for food
and weaving, which is for clothing
and building
and it is for dwelling
and governance, which is for union, association, and cooperation over the means of livelihood and their regulation

The second: those that prepare for each one of these crafts and serve it, like blacksmithing, for it serves farming and a number of crafts by preparing their tools, and like carding and spinning, for they serve weaving by preparing its work.

The third: those that complete the foundations and adorn them, like milling and baking for farming, and like fulling and tailoring for weaving. In relation to the subsistence of the affair of the earthly world, this is like the parts of a person in relation to the whole of him, for these too are of three kinds: either foundations, like the heart, the liver, and the brain; or those that serve them, like the stomach, the vessels, the arteries, the nerves, and the veins; or those that complete and adorn them, like the nails, the fingers, and the eyebrows. The noblest of these crafts are their foundations, and the noblest of their foundations is governance, through union and reform. Because of that, this craft calls for a perfection in whoever takes charge of it that the other crafts do not call for; and because of that, the one who holds this craft inevitably employs all the other craftsmen. Governance, in the reform of people and their guidance to the straight path that saves in this world and the Hereafter, has four ranks. The first, which is the highest, is the governance of the prophets (peace be upon them) and their rule over the elite and the common people alike, in their outward side and their inward side.
And the second is the caliphs, kings, and sultans, and their rule over the elite and the common people alike, but over their outward side and not their inward side.

And the third is the scholars with knowledge of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and of His religion, who are the heirs of the prophets, and their rule is over the inward side of the elite only. The understanding of the common people does not rise to benefiting from them, and their power does not reach as far as acting upon the outward side of either by compulsion, prohibition, and legislation.

And the fourth is the preachers, and their rule is over the inward side of the common people only. The noblest of these four crafts after prophethood is imparting knowledge, refining people's selves from the blameworthy, destructive character traits, and guiding them to the praiseworthy, felicity-giving character traits, and this is what is meant by teaching. We said that this is more excellent than the rest of the trades and crafts because the nobility of crafts is known by three matters: either by regard to the innate faculty by which knowledge of them is reached, like the superiority of the rational intellects over the linguistic ones, since wisdom is perceived by the intellect and language by hearing, and the intellect is nobler than hearing; or by looking to the generality of benefit, like the superiority of farming over goldsmithing; or by attending to the thing worked upon, like the superiority of goldsmithing over tanning, since what is worked upon in one is gold and in the other the skin of carrion. And it is not hidden that the religious sciences, which are the understanding (fiqh) of the path of the Hereafter, are perceived only through the perfection of the intellect and the purity of intelligence, and the intellect is the noblest of the attributes of the human being, as its explanation will come, for by it the trust of Allah is accepted and by it the vicinity of Allah, glorified is He, is reached.
As for the generality of benefit, there is no doubt about it, for its benefit and fruit is the happiness of the Hereafter.

As for the nobility of what is worked upon, how could it be hidden, when the teacher works upon the hearts and selves of human beings, and the noblest existent on earth is the human kind, and the noblest part of the essential parts of the human being is his heart, and the teacher is occupied with perfecting it, polishing it, purifying it, and leading it to nearness to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic? So teaching knowledge is, in one respect, worship of Allah Most High, and in another respect, vicegerency (khilafa) of Allah Most High, and it is among the most sublime forms of vicegerency of Allah. For Allah Most High has opened upon the heart of the scholar the knowledge that is the most particular of His attributes, so he is like the keeper of His most precious treasuries; then he is permitted to spend from it on everyone who needs it. What rank is more sublime than that a servant be an intermediary between his Lord, glorified is He, and His creation, in bringing them near to Allah in closeness and leading them to the Paradise of Refuge? May Allah make us among them by His generosity, and may Allah send blessings upon every chosen servant.

nilai.catatan: Judul bagian setia dan lengkap.
Pelaku (yang berharap mengetahui kebijaksanaan Zayd) dan jangkauan negasi 'belum memahami' tepat; kalimat terakhir ada.
Isi setia dan lengkap; hanya 'additional growth' untuk sil'a bisa terbaca sebagai pertumbuhan ukuran, bukan benjolan, dan 'to anything' pada 'without relation' tidak ada di sumber.
Tiga pembagian dengan urutan sumber, dirham dan dinar sebagai batu yang tak bermanfaat, serta kalimat penutup lengkap.
Setia: kebahagiaan akhirat dan kenikmatan memandang wajah Allah dicari karena dirinya sendiri.
Contoh kaki, kedekatan hanya dicapai lewat ilmu, rantai ilmu-amal-kebahagiaan, dan tiga buah ilmu semuanya tepat.
Pelaku dan objek tepat (orang Turki dan Arab menghormati para sesepuh, hewan menghormati manusia); kalimat penutup tentang perbedaan ilmu ada.
Dalil belajar-mengajar, dunia sebagai ladang akhirat, 'alat' bagi yang menjadikannya alat dan 'tempat tinggal' bagi yang menjadikannya tempat menetap sesuai sumber.
Kalimat lanjutan, tiga bagian.
Fragmen: bagian pertama, empat pokok, pertanian untuk makanan.
Fragmen: penenunan untuk pakaian.
Fragmen pendek 'dan bangunan'.
Fragmen: bangunan itu untuk tempat tinggal.
Fragmen: pemerintahan untuk menyatukan, berhimpun, dan bekerja sama atas sarana hidup serta penataannya.
Bagian kedua: pandai besi melayani pertanian dan sejumlah kerajinan, pengurai kapas dan pemintal melayani penenunan; pelaku dan objek tepat.

Bagian ketiga, perumpamaan anggota badan (pokok, pelayan, penyempurna), empat tingkat, dan tingkat pertama (para nabi atas semua orang, lahir dan batin) tepat; 'side' dipakai konsisten untuk lahir/batin.
Tingkat kedua: penguasa atas lahir kedua golongan, bukan batin; negasi tepat.
Tingkat ketiga dan negasi lengkap; kata ganti 'zawahirihim' diputuskan jadi 'of either', pilihan yang masuk akal tetapi menutup ambiguitas sumber, dan 'acting upon' untuk tasarruf lemah.

Tingkat keempat, tiga tolok ukur kemuliaan, dan kalimat penutup lengkap dan setia pada teks tercetak; 'rational intellects over the linguistic ones' janggal karena kemungkinan salah cetak untuk 'sciences'.
Keluasan manfaat tidak diragukan; buahnya kebahagiaan akhirat.
Guru bekerja pada hati, ilmu dibuka Allah pada hati orang alim, perantara hamba dan Tuhan, doa penutup; 'them' dan 'chosen servant' sesuai sumber.
